data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims there is no safe recovery path for mid-event interruption under strict append-only semantics, presenting a false dichotomy: either reference the partial event (invalid) or rewrite it (violates append-only). It entirely omits the standard append-only recovery mechanism of appending an abort/tombstone marker after the partial event. An abort marker is itself an atomic, append-only event with a stable identity that tombstones the partial record without referencing it as a causal parent, allowing a fresh event to be appended afterward. Because appending such a marker does not rewrite the partial event and preserves append-only identity, the claim that 'refusal is the only responsible action' fails to determine the exact conditions under which resumption is safely possible, falsely over-constraining the refusal criteria.
